newsitem.title: UK: Export activity keeps wheat markets on the boil.
newsitem.headline: Export activity keeps wheat markets on the boil.

text.p: Export demand for wheat continued to occupy traders' attention in Chicago and European grain markets on Thursday while a nervous copper market kept London Metal Exchange traders on their toes.

Grain exporters started off the day by bidding for more than a million tonnes of export licenses at the EU's weekly tender, pushing European prices higher as rumours flooded the market of substantial business to various destinations in North Africa, East Europe, and the Middle East.

"There's been a feeling for a couple of days that there is some business around," a UK trader said. He noted that the enquiries were coming from shippers, especially those with a potential interest in selling to eastern Europe.

On the UKs grain futures market, January wheat gained 1.5 sterling a tonne to 96.25 stg a tonne before an EU announcement it had awarded export licenses for only 477,700 tonnes of wheat cut gains in late trading.

Chicago followed up with December wheat futures on the Board of Trade gaining five cents to $4.04 a bushel on news of India's requirement for two million tonnes of wheat in the near term to augment domestic supplies.
London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices fluctuated nervously with some traders concerned their may be a short sharp squeeze on supplies of metal available for delivery next week.
But others reckoned that LME copper stocks could rise by up to 10,000 tonnes on Friday which would provide some relief to the market.
The three months delivery copper price swung around in a $40 a tonne range until ending at $2,148, virtually unchanged from Wednesday.
Also on the LME the lead price soared to $700 a tonne as some buying orders from the far east brought in speculative demand for the metal.
Traders said some of the buying was in anticipation that demand for the metal from battery manufacturers in the Northern Hemisphere would pick-up after a slow start to the season.
